name: Maadja
title: Priest in Nehemiah's time
summary: Maadja (also spelled Maadiah or Maadja) was one of the priests who returned to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel after the Babylonian exile. He is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as part of the priestly families that served in the rebuilt temple service. His descendants continued the priesthood in subsequent generations.

keyEvents.title: Return from exile with Zerubbabel
keyEvents.description: Maadja was one of the priests who returned to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel and Joshua (Jeshua) after the Babylonian exile.

keyEvents.title: Registration among the priestly families
keyEvents.description: Maadja was registered as head of one of the priestly families that served in Jerusalem after returning from Babylon.

keyEvents.title: Priestly service in the rebuilt temple
keyEvents.description: Maadja and the other priests helped restore the lawful temple service in Jerusalem after the exile.

keyEvents.title: Descendant Piltaj serves as priest
keyEvents.description: In the next generation, Piltaj was head of Maadjas' priestly line in the days of Jehoiakim.
